 ],

  {'name': ns+'roundedProductTree', 'description': 'For each model m, a function P_m:T(R x R)->T(R) mapping a leaf (a,b) to roundedProductTerm(m,a,b)=Model.mul(m,a,b)=r(a*b).  ],
 'assumptions': [

  'Every quantified model supplies u in R with 0<=u and r:R->R such that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta|<=u and r(z)=z*(1+delta). The error delta may depend on z. No particular floating-point format, representable set, or rounding rule is specified beyond this property.',
  'The relation I_B is the inductively generated relation with leaf rule |y-x|<=B*|x| and node rule that combines the two child relations using the same bound B. B has domain R; nonnegativity is not a separate premise of its definition.',
  'In roundedDotProduct_exists_perturbation, in addition to being a model and a pair-labelled tree, the hypotheses are (d(t)+1)*u<1 and the entire existential assertion that is repeated verbatim as the conclusion.   'The natural parameter k=d(t)+1 is coerced to R in gamma(k,u)=(k*u)/(1-k*u) and in the strict depth bound. Gamma is supplied as a function on N x R with no defining domain restriction; the theorem separately imposes k*u<1, ensuring a positive denominator in its use here.',

 ],
